algorithms.name: BOLD (Black-box Online Learning under Delayed feedback)

symbols.G_star: E[G*_n], expected maximum number of outstanding feedbacks during the first n steps
symbols.f_Base: nondecreasing concave (expected) regret bound of the non-delayed base algorithm, f(0)=0

conditions: delays tau_t independent of the forecaster's predictions
base algorithm enjoys (expected) regret bound f_Base in the non-delayed problem

source.label: thm:BOLD-Expected-Bound
source.quote: Suppose that the non-delayed algorithm \Base used in BOLD enjoys an (expected) regret bound $f_\Base$. Assume, furthermore, that the delays $\tau_t$ are independent of the forecaster's prediction $a_t$. Then the expected regret of BOLD after $n$ time steps satisfies \ExpVal{R_n} \le \ExpVal{(G^*_n+1) f_\Base(n/(G^*_n+1))} \le (\ExpVal{G^*_n}+1) f_\Base(n/(\ExpVal{G^*_n}+1)).

results.notes: Recorded the second (weaker, deterministic-argument) inequality. Meta-result; constant delay case recovers Weinberger & Ordentlich. Horizon depends on base algorithm.

symbols.f_Base: nondecreasing concave (expected) regret bound of the non-delayed base algorithm

conditions: delays i.i.d. with finite expectation, independent of predictions
base algorithm enjoys (expected) regret bound f_Base

source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:BOLD-Expected-Bound}, if the sequence of delays is i.i.d, then \[ \ExpVal{R_n} \le (B(n,\ExpVal{\tau_1})+2) f_\Base\left(\dfrac{n}{B(n,\ExpVal{\tau_1})+2}\right). \]

symbols.R_Base: expected regret of the base algorithm run in the same environment without delays for n steps
symbols.G_i: E[G*_{i,n}], expected maximum number of missing feedbacks for arm i up to time n

conditions: feedback/reward sequences of different predictions independent

source.label: thm:Q-Alg-Expected-Regret
source.quote: Suppose the non-delayed \Base algorithm is used in \StochBlackBoxAlg in a delayed stochastic IPM environment. Then the expected regret of \StochBlackBoxAlg is upper-bounded by \ExpVal{R_n} \le \ExpVal{ R^\textsc{Base}_n } + \sum_{i=1}^{K} \Delta_i \ExpVal{ G^*_{i,n} }

results.notes: Regret defined as sum Delta_i E[T_i(n)], hence pseudo-regret. With bounded delays G*_{i,n} <= tau_max.

symbols.G_i: E[G*_{i,n}], expected maximum number of missing feedbacks for arm i up to time n

source.label: thm:UCB-Delayed-Expected-Bound
source.quote: For any $n \ge 1$, the expected regret of the Delayed-UCB1 algorithm is bounded by \ExpVal{R_n} \le \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0}\left[ \dfrac{8 \log{n}}{\Delta_i} + 3.5\Delta_i \right] + \sum_{i=1}^{K} \Delta_i \ExpVal{G_{i,n}^*}.

results.notes: Bounded [0,1] rewards implicit via UCB1/Hoeffding analysis.

symbols.G_i: E[G*_{i,n}], expected maximum number of missing feedbacks for arm i

tuning: exploration function log t + 3 log log t

source.label: thm:KL-UCB
source.quote: For any $\epsilon > 0$, the expected regret of the Delayed-KL-UCB algorithm after $n$ time instants satisfies \ExpVal {R_n} \le \sum_{i: \Delta_i>0}^{} \Delta_i (\dfrac{\log(n)}{\kldiv(\mu_i,\mu_{i^*})} (1 + \epsilon) + C_1 \log(\log(n)) ) + \sum_{i=1}^{K} \Delta_i (\dfrac{C_2(\epsilon)}{n^{\beta(\epsilon)}} \ExpVal{G^*_{i,n}} +\ExpVal{G^*_{i,n}} + 1)
